The mouth is labeled Bocana Río Micay. The coverage map differentiates mixed/guandal inland forest and coastal mangrove belts.

sources.title: Gander River—A Stream Inventory
sources.author: Gerald R. Traverse
sources.publisher_or_host: Department of the Environment, Fisheries Service, Resource Development Branch, Newfoundland Region; official DFO Waves repository
sources.source_type: Primary original field-survey cartography with bounded supporting prose.
sources.map_locator: Figure1, printed p.2/PDF p.8; cover, title, methods and watershed description pp.1,3–4 also read.
sources.observed_scope: Northwest/Southwest Gander distinction, lake connection, lower pond sequence and Gander Bay ending. Headward fork correspondence remains incomplete.
sources.use_notice: The inspected cover/title and searchable report text expose no citation-permission or limited-distribution warning. This is distinct from excluded DFO Research Document97/37 on Humber. No permission to redistribute original maps or crops is inferred.

correspondence.finding: The selected opening is within the northern headward stream network on the high ground west of the separately labeled Kirchoffer River. A continuous southward narrow stream and tributary junctions lead into the valley carrying the Boas River label. The opening is not inferred only from proximity to that label.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: A separate hydronym for the initial short headward component is unestablished; representative system identity does not extend the river label uniformly to every feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper valley and main lowland bend
correspondence.finding: The route follows the mapped southward Boas valley east of Mount Saorre, the westward turn by The Buttocks and the connected northwestward lowland swing. The source shows the actual channel, small inflows and intervening widened water, distinct from the thematic wildlife/ecological boundaries.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Boas River is directly printed on the upper river; mountain and thematic-unit names are not used as hydronyms.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad unnamed lake and tributary junction
correspondence.finding: After the northwest/west lowland swing the river turns south, reaches the eastern side of a broad irregular lake, crosses its connected water and leaves by the southern arm. The lake is shown with a180-foot water elevation but no inspected lake name. The separately labeled Salmon Pond and Sutton drainage lie east of this passage, with their connecting tributary depicted separately. Northern and eastern tributary connections do not interrupt the selected lake-to-river interpretation.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: The broad lake remains unnamed here; Salmon Pond and the Sutton tributary are not relabeled as Boas River or treated as a mandatory passage of this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern river widening and sheet join
correspondence.finding: The lake outlet continues south through a widened, islanded and locally branching Boas corridor, then southwest. The adjacent sheets show the same connected river across their shared border, with numerous nearby lakes and wetland channels. No reservoir or separately named intervening lake is required to explain this portion.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Boas labels support the representative river; the names of individual islands, short anabranches and minor pools remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Delta, distributaries and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The lower river broadens and splits among islands and lowland/tidal channels within the historically labeled Harry Gibbons Migratory Bird Sanctuary. The selected southwesterly continuation reaches the western part of the Boas delta/estuary, with mapped distributaries opening onto extensive tidal flats at the northern end of Bay of Gods Mercy. The separate Unhealing Brook enters the bay east of the Boas distributary complex and is not the selected terminal river. The ECCC account independently describes the lower Boas delta, estuary and adjacent tidal flats.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: The complete system candidate is Boas River, while the selected final distributary has no separately established proper name. No exact modern tidal boundary, unique mouth vertex or present flow partition is asserted.

correspondence.finding: All selected model parts were read for orientation. No original primary map acquired establishes the southern opening or its entire north-trending mountain corridor.

Primary prose distinguishes the Jolí and Micay sectors south of López de Micay and the separate Chuare-to-Micay relationship. Local thematic mapping cannot establish the whole selected middle continuation and actual junction placement.
correspondence.correspondence: insufficient local context; full fragment unresolved

correspondence.finding: The lower original base and coverage maps show the Micay receiving corridor, Noanamito bifurcation, separate western outlets, eastern Quebrada Tambor connection, coastal mangroves and northern Bocana Río Micay. The selected coastal form is consistent with this network at ordinary corridor scale; the entire inland start of this fragment is not positively linked.
correspondence.correspondence: partial lower/coastal corridor positive; inland opening unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Far-eastern opening and initial southward turn followed by northwestward feeder
correspondence.finding: The retained selection begins east of the La Moinerie–Guers lake setting and turns from its initial southerly opening into a northwestward course. This is model orientation only. The inspected regional original does not distinguish this exact initial feeder and all intervening lake/stream links; its initial geographic connection remains unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Approach to the La Moinerie and Guers lake setting
correspondence.finding: The original regional map distinguishes the rounded Lac La Moinerie and the more complex Lac Guers north of it. These are geographic context for the selected central-eastern sector. The selected approach, actual lake entry/exit and continuous inter-lake connector have not all been distinguished in original cartography; no unverified selected lake traversal is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lake/outlet turns toward the Marralik corridor
correspondence.finding: The original shows the La Moinerie–Guers setting east of Lac Saffray and a northward Marralik drainage. It does not resolve the selected westward lake arm/outlet, the intervening river junction and the actual joining relation at ordinary component scale. Discovery-only Danguy and other reach names are not used as map evidence.

CEHQ2011 repeatedly labels Rivière Marralik along a separate drainage east of Rivière à la Baleine and west of Rivière Qurlutuq. This supports a broad Marralik corridor candidate for the selected northward continuation. The original is generalized and does not establish every selected widening, material lateral junction or intervening lake identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Final lower outlet and actual receiving-water setting
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the Marralik drainage approaching southern Ungava Bay east of the separate Rivière à la Baleine estuarine setting. The available map does not distinguish the selected final channel and its actual coastal receiving-water connection sufficiently to complete terminal correspondence. No precise estuary-mouth or island relation is inferred from uninspected records or the model sea classification.

finding: The selected opening is considered against the complete survey map but is not securely assigned to one depicted headward fork.
The remaining broad corridor corresponds to Northwest Gander approaching Gander Lake; Great Gull is a separate tributary. Southwest Gander enters the lake separately.
correspondence.correspondence: Partial; initial headward pond/feeder connector unresolved.
correspondence.unresolved: Specific initial pond/feeder path and its connection into the observed Northwest Gander trunk.

finding: The route crosses the western Gander Lake setting to its outlet near Glenwood, then follows the lower Gander.
The mapped lower river passes Fourth, Third, Second and First ponds, with separate tributary branches, and enters Gander Bay.
